faq.a: Azamat is associated with the Arabic form عَزَمَت, whose core sense is azamat; greatness, majesty.

faq.q: What is the origin of Azamat?
faq.a: Azamat is associated with Arabic. Azamat is Arabic عَظَمَة (ʿAẓama), meaning 'greatness, majesty'. It is widely used as a male given name in Central Asia and the Caucasus.
Yes — the underlying form عَزَمَت is Arabic.
Azamat can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Azamat should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. The root ع ظ م is Quranic (greatness), but ʿAẓamat is not itself a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Azamat mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Azamat is rendered عزمت and carries the sense عزمت، عظمت.

faq.q: What does Azamat mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Azamat is rendered عظمت and carries the sense عظمت، بزرگی.
A romanized syllable approximation is a-za-mat. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Azamat?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Azamat, azamat. Script forms are عزمت, عظمت, عَزَمَت, अज़मत.

faq.q: Is Azamat a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
